title: Subway Violin
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk, violinist Suwan（A woman violinist in her thirties, black beret, black performance coat, violin in left hand and bow in right, focused expression） enters the subway concourse（A brightly lit subway concourse, pillars plastered with ads, echo mixing announcements, footsteps, and violin） and takes the Nightingale violin（An amber old violin, a tiny nightingale carved on the scroll, bright strings, varnish with fine growth-ring grain） from its velvet bag to tune.

Five emergency lights（A row of five green emergency lights under the concourse beam, clear covers, auto-lit in blackout） glow under the concourse beam; Suwan looks up to confirm they will not glare on the violin face.

Two signal bells（Two departure signal bells by the gates, metal shells polished bright, short chimes before trains arrive） hang by the gates; before a train arrives they chime briefly, and Suwan stops the bow to let the sound pass.
Suwan sets the Nightingale violin on her shoulder; the first melody echoes along the ad pillars.

Suwan unties the ribbon, opens the repertoire notebook（A hard-cover repertoire notebook holding a subway map, performance-permit copies, and set order）, and writes the rush-hour set beside the subway map.
She glances at the five emergency lights under the beam, then clips the permit copy back into the repertoire notebook.
Suwan closes the repertoire notebook, sets the Nightingale violin back on its pad, and waits for the next train's noise to pass.

At the dawn platform edge（Beside the yellow platform line, wind surging from the tunnel, next-train times flashing on signs above the screen doors）, Suwan greets young Shuanger（A fifteen-year-old apprentice girl, indigo scarf, silver stud in left ear, carrying a violin case nearly half her height） pushing the folding violin-case cart（A black folding violin-case cart, nightingale sticker on the case face, handle intact, wheels free）; screen doors mirror both shadows.
Shuanger parks the folding violin-case cart outside the yellow line, locks a wheel, nightingale sticker facing the platform sign.

Suwan lays out three rosin cakes（Three amber rosin cakes in a paper box on the case lid, corners rubbed white by the bow） on the case lid and teaches Shuanger to tell new, old, and broken rosin apart.
Shuanger crouches to check the folding violin-case cart handle hinge, making sure it will not loose in a crowd.

In the transfer corridor（A long transfer corridor, escalators humming, tile walls gleaming, crowds like tide, transfer arrows on the floor）, Axi（A young woman violinist nearly identical in face to Shuanger, but with a silver-gray sleeve band and charcoal-black scarf, showy look） with a silver-gray sleeve band glances back from tile glare; her profile almost looks like Shuanger.
Axi wraps her charcoal-black scarf tight and bends to adjust her portable pickup.
Axi carries a light violin bag through the far transfer arrows, dodging the morning crowd.
Beside the yellow platform line, Shuanger and Axi brush past—one in indigo scarf, one with silver-gray sleeve band.
Shuanger steadies her silver stud; Axi presses her charcoal scarf; two similar faces turn toward the train lights together.
After the train leaves, they split at different stair mouths; their backs are cut in two by the platform sign.
Months later on a leak night, Suwan packs the violin spot alone in the subway concourse; the Nightingale violin leans by a pillar.

Condensate from the ceiling drips into the repertoire notebook（The same repertoire notebook soaked by underground damp: cover wrinkled, map corners curled, set lists bled）; map corners curl and set-list ink bleeds in the damp.
Suwan clips the repertoire notebook behind an ad board to dry, then wipes mist from the Nightingale violin strings.
The performance season stretches on; every day Suwan finds gaps between announcements to play in the subway concourse.
In the morning rush she softens the tone as commuters stream past.
At high summer noon, AC drips in the concourse; Suwan wipes fine mist from the top plate.
Through autumn rain, pillar ads rotate three times; the Nightingale violin still hangs on her shoulder.
After the last New Year's Eve train, Suwan alone finishes one more piece facing the empty concourse.
At dawn, Suwan patrols the platform edge; the folding violin-case cart sits outside the yellow line, wheel lock tight.
She crouches to check the folding violin-case cart handle, hinge, and small wheels, ducking a gust from an arriving train.
Suwan returns to the concourse violin spot and confirms those three rosin cakes are still in the paper box.

Staff push a yellow-plate luggage cart（A yellow-numbered station luggage cart with no nightingale sticker, open bed, nothing like the folding violin-case cart） across the platform, bed open, no nightingale sticker at all.
Rush hour blacks out suddenly; crowds pack the platform edge; signs above the screen doors flicker.

Suwan backs up guarding the Nightingale violin（The same Nightingale violin, a long crack in the top plate, varnish peeling beside the nightingale carving, tone hollow）; a corner hits a metal bench and a thin crack opens in the top plate.
The folding violin-case cart is shoved toward the yellow line; the wheel lock pops and the case sticker scrapes the tiles.

The folding violin-case cart（The folding violin-case cart crushed by a station repair tractor: case face burst, handle bent, nightingale sticker torn） slides into the repair zone and is crushed by a station repair tractor; handle bent, nightingale sticker shattered.
Suwan holds the cracked Nightingale violin and retreats by a pillar, signaling Shuanger not to chase that cart.
The day after the blackout, Suwan writes the time the folding violin-case cart was crushed on a blank page of the repertoire notebook.
A remnant nightingale sticker from the folding violin-case cart is stuck by a concourse pillar; Suwan gathers the scraps into an envelope.
Suwan clips a photo of the folding violin-case cart's broken handle into the repertoire notebook to warn Shuanger away from the yellow line.
The five emergency lights under the beam still glow; Suwan reads the folding violin-case cart accident record by green light.
Tape covers the Nightingale violin crack; Suwan notes beside the notebook the last platform number of the folding violin-case cart.
Weeks later, Suwan brings a luthier to spread felt in a concourse rest corner, ready to patch the Nightingale violin.

The luthier first sets out a replica violin（A glossy replica violin shaped like the Nightingale violin, but no nightingale carving and a plastic bridge） for contrast—gloss similar, but no nightingale carving, plastic bridge.
Suwan watches the luthier press new wood into the crack; strings hang loose to one side for now.

After the patch, the Nightingale violin（The Nightingale violin after patch repair: new wood set into the crack, nightingale carving still there, tone slightly muted） crack is steadied by new wood; Suwan gently tests a slightly muted tone.

A cleaner pushes the cleaning cart（A gray cleaning cart hung with mop and trash bags, neither violin-case handle nor nightingale sticker） to the platform edge; only mop and trash bags on it—no violin-case handle.

The station supervisor（A lean station supervisor in a dark coat too, but with metro armband and walkie-talkie on the chest, build close to Suwan's） walks up beside Suwan, also in a dark coat, but the walkie-talkie on his chest keeps flashing.
The station supervisor points at the cleaning cart and warns her to yield; Suwan holds the patched Nightingale violin steadier.

From the transfer corridor comes flower-seller Xiaoyu（A flower-selling girl in the transfer corridor, light-brown scarf; at a glance like young Shuanger, but with wireless in-ear monitor and shy eyes）; under a light-brown scarf her profile at a glance looks like young Shuanger.
When Xiaoyu offers flowers her wireless in-ear shows; Suwan only asks her to avoid the crowd by the violin spot.

At dusk years later, Suwan（The same Suwan: right wrist wrapped in a support bandage, bow tucked in her elbow, coat cuff frayed, still wearing the black beret） with a bandaged right wrist alone enters the sealed abandoned platform（A sealed abandoned platform, broken tubes, rusted rails, faded curling posters, dusty benches）.
Two old signal bells still hang by the abandoned-platform gates; Suwan stops to hear them clink in the draft.
Suwan presses her bowless right hand to the cold bench, as if saying goodbye to this concourse.

By day, adult Shuanger（A woman violinist in her early twenties, still in indigo scarf and silver stud, upright build, old music bag on her shoulder） returns along the transfer corridor; the indigo scarf sways lightly in the empty-platform wind.
By the abandoned-platform bench Shuanger steadies wrist-injured Suwan and takes her old music bag.
Beside the bench, Shuanger holds Suwan's cold hand and hears where the performance permit plaque hangs.
Suwan（Suwan has closed her eyes forever, lying still on a abandoned-platform bench, performance coat over her chest, bow at her side）'s breath fades; at last she closes her eyes and dies in silence.
Suwan's black beret still hangs in the abandoned-platform locker; Shuanger brushes the dust away.

Adult Shuanger rehangs the performance permit plaque（A small brass plaque on a concourse pillar, engraved with 'Su violin spot', permit number, and station name） on a concourse pillar; Suwan's permit number is still engraved.
Shuanger traces Suwan's name on the performance permit plaque, then sets the patched Nightingale violin at the center of the violin spot.

Remade Axi（Remade Axi still wears the silver-gray sleeve band; a string-pressure mark on her brow ridge, charcoal scarf swapped for a short cape） walks in from outside the abandoned platform; silver-gray sleeve band still on her left arm, facing Shuanger across the yellow line.
Shuanger and Axi stand side by side before the bench—one calm in indigo scarf, one with a short cape over a dark violin bag.
The shot returns to years ago—the girl in indigo scarf learning to apply rosin by the case appears again.
The opening moment returns—the amber violin with a nightingale carved on the scroll first rests against the shoulder.
Flash back to an early transfer corridor—a figure with silver-gray sleeve band and charcoal scarf flashes through tile glare.
Again five green lights under the beam light an empty-concourse old night.
Back to the yellow line of first meeting; tunnel wind stirs the signs, as if it just happened.
Shuanger opens the damp-blurred repertoire notebook and resets the rush-hour set in the subway concourse.
The five emergency lights under the beam still glow; Shuanger counts them, then dims the violin-spot lightbox.
Those three rosin cakes are still in the paper box on the case lid; Shuanger draws the first phrase on the patched Nightingale violin.
